blocks.text: Real Russian sentences that use what the lesson teaches. Type the missing word, or pick it, until it turns green.

These are real sentences: from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR), with their English translations, and from the public-domain Russian books in this library, with author and title. Each blank is the word the sentence really has; the word in brackets is its dictionary form.

exercises.why: «Certain adjectives have irregular comparatives»: выше, ниже, шире, короче, легче, глубже, дороже, дешевле, лучше, хуже, больше, меньше, старше, моложе … — DLI, Lessons 80–82. From Александр Серафимович, «Железный поток».

exercises.ru: Обхватил крестник еще крепче ___ за колено и слезами заплакал.
exercises.why: «An adjective in the comparative degree may be followed by the object of comparison in the Genitive case, or by a phrase consisting of "чем" plus the object of comparison in the Nominative case.» — DLI, Lesson 80. From Лев Толстой, «Крестник».
«The comparative degree of Russian adjectives is formed by adding "-ее" (sometimes shortened to "-ей") to the stem of the adjective.» — DLI, Lesson 80. From Викентий Вересаев, «На войне».
